newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Woolwich ups insurance activities.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Woolwich ups insurance activities.

text.p: Britain's third largest building society, the Woolwich, on Wednesday announced a major drive into general insurance in 1997.

The Woolwich, which intends to float on the London stock market in July, is to use its joint venture insurance operation with Legal & General as a springboard to expand distribution and develop the traditional products it offers such as buildings and contents insurance.
It also plans to introduce new lines such as motor and travel insurance.

Existing insurance services contributed over 11 million pounds ($18.41 million) profit in the first nine months of last year and group operations director Lynne Peacock said there was strong organic growth potential in the insurance area.
"We've done our homework and now we are ready for the step change in our general insurance activities," said Peacock.

The move. part of the group's diversification strategy, is unlikely to be welcomed by traditional insurance providers, already under pressure from falling rates and growing competition in an increasingly fragmented market.
Halifax Building Society has made similar moves, part of a growing trend of building societies seeking to capture more of the insurance market.

"It is a worry for the industry. Everbody seems to want to be an insurance provider whether they're a building society, bank, Sainsbury or Tesco and its putting a big strain on margins," said one industry analyst.
Woolwich's move is to be spearheaded through its Woolwich Insurance Services (WIS) company, the sales and marketing vehicle of the joint venture with Legal & General.

While in the past the building society has typically arranged household insurance for around 75 percent of its eligible borrowers, less than one percent of Woolwich's 3.5 million investing customers currently buy insurance from it.

The half a million existing policies at WIS almost exclusively cover household insurance and the aim for 1997 is to sell around 100,000 comletely new policies -- travel and motor policies and contents insurance to Woolwich investors.

"Having started from simply selling existing insurance companies' products and taking a brokerage fee, building societies are looking to expand into the more administrative areas and ultimately perhaps begin underwriting," said UBS building society analyst Rob Thomas.
Specialist general insurance advisers for every high street branch are planned by the Woolwich by year end and its new travel insurance, Holidaywise, will be available in UK branches from January 20.
Woolwich motor insurance will be on offer from the end of the month and the company is also planning to develop a direct telephone operation.
